known_limitations: Empty files with a secret-like name (e.g. an empty server.key) are not reported: gitleaks skips empty files. They carry no secret material; the old scanner reported them.
Archives (zip/gz) are not unpacked (--max-archive-depth 0), as in M0.

The default gitleaks rules run with gitleaks' default allowlist (skips *.bin, *.pdf, images, node_modules/, ...). The AC-M0-04 rules run in .gitleaks-strict.toml without it; other default rules (API tokens) do not see those paths.

.gitleaksignore pins 7 historical findings by fingerprint (commit:path:rule:line): the two old (path, blob) pairs (5 findings: reports/conformance/M0.json@9d34699, reports/critic/M0-cycle-1.json@3182606) and 2 default-rule false positives in history (Ed25519PrivateKey type name @52874f5, fake key body of the deleted test @f5cf832). One extra allowlist: SHA-256 digests in tests/contract/schema-lock.json for generic-api-key.
The config, ignore file and wrapper come from the PR head, as the old scanner did: a PR can weaken them. CODEOWNERS marks them as owned (no required review, owner decision).
gitleaks.sh downloads linux x64 only; elsewhere set GITLEAKS to a local 8.30.1 binary (version checked).
mutmut cannot follow subprocesses; the subprocess tests are marked e2e and deselected under mutmut, the logic they drive is tested in-process. run_contract_tests is covered by a fake contract tree.

`# pragma: no mutate` on the three ensure_ascii lines also hides the non-equivalent False->True mutant; tests/ci/test_schema_lock_cli.py pins non-ASCII hashing and rendering, so that mutant would be killed.
